note: Pinned candidate artifacts for raster qualification (Q). Installed only into an isolated bench directory; never into a production manifest. The integrity values are the npm registry sha512 digests recorded in the bench lock file.

sourceToArtifactCorrespondence.finding: Each pinned source commit is published under a different semver than its Cargo.toml version, and the artifact whose gitHead matches the pin is not the one the plan's text names. Verified by reading the npm registry metadata (gitHead) for every published version.

whitebox-wasm.detail: No published whitebox-wasm artifact has gitHead 9c0ff4f. 0.5.1 (gitHead 6920ade) is the newest published artifact and predates the pin; the pin's manifest already declares 0.6.0, which is unpublished.

cog-tiler-wasm.detail: cog-tiler-wasm@0.3.6 gitHead is exactly the pinned commit. The plan's inspected '0.3.1' is a different commit (770519f4) and is also the wrong artifact to pair with whitebox-wasm 0.5.1.

peerResolution.finding: The naive install of the two artifacts named in the plan fails, and the natural modern resolution is also broken. Both were reproduced.

attempts.outcome: npm ERESOLVE: peer whitebox-wasm@^0.4.1 from cog-tiler-wasm@0.3.1
runtime failure: the module no longer provides a default export, so cog-tiler's `geokeysToProj4.toProj4` is undefined

working: cog-tiler-wasm@0.3.6 peers whitebox-wasm@^0.4.1 || ^0.5.1, so 0.5.1 is admitted
geotiff-geokeys-to-proj4 must be pinned to 2024.4.13 (the ^2024.4.13 alternative), which still exports a default
